reject_kind: sequencing (hold), not code quality: the two commits are correct as written and may land unchanged once the accumulator miscompile is fixed
reasons: BLOCKER (item 4, confirmed): llvm/lib/Target/RISCV/Snitch/SNITCHFrepLoops.cpp convertToHardwareLoop (back-edge removal ~l.613-660; fixupPHIs call commented out at ~l.742) miscompiles every loop-carried FP value. Reviewer repro with build/20-F033, -mcpu=snitch, the README example (README.md:241-245) under '#pragma frep infer': at -O1/-O2/-O3/-Os the output is 'fcvt.d.w fa5,zero; li a0,127; frep.o a0,1,0,0; fmadd.d fa0,ft0,ft1,fa5' - every iteration reads the initial 0, so the function returns the last product, not the dot product. ref-18 and int-20 with -mllvm -snitch-frep-inference and no pragma produce the same instructions, so the bug is pre-existing. Cause: the pass deletes the back edge but leaves the header PHI '%1 = PHI %5, %bb.0, %2, %bb.2' (bb.2 is no longer its own predecessor), so nothing forces the accumulator's def and use into one register. llc -O2 -verify-machineinstrs reports bad machine code; llc -O0 without optnone happens to allocate 'fmadd.d fa5,ft0,ft1,fa5' (correct by luck). Two accumulators in one loop are also wrong: 'fmadd.d fa5,ft0,ft1,fa4' reads s1's register. A loop with no carried value (SSR push of pop+pop) is correct. llvm/test/CodeGen/RISCV/freploop.ll hwloop2 only checks 'fmadd.d {{.*}}', so it cannot catch this.

RECOMMENDATION on item 4: do not land F033 before the accumulator bug is fixed. Today '#pragma frep infer' is a hard compile error on every build (ref-18 and int-20), which fails safe. With F033 alone the documented spelling, on the README's own example, compiles silently to a wrong result. FREP's main use is reductions (dot products, GEMM inner loops). '-snitch-frep-inference' being reachable already does not make this acceptable: it is a hidden -mllvm developer flag, while the pragma is the documented user interface. AGENT_RULES 'a guessed fix that lands is the worst outcome' applies even more to a silent miscompile. Next step: a passes-cluster task (backlog row, owner SNITCHFrepLoops) that makes the pass handle a loop-carried FP PHI correctly: keep the accumulator in one register, e.g. with a tied def/use or by rewriting the PHI into a copy the allocator must coalesce, and add a verify-clean MIR check. Or, as an interim, it makes the pass decline such loops. Declining turns off frep for the README example, so under the escalation rules it is an owner decision. Land F033 after that task, or together with it. No change to F033's own commits is needed.

NOTE (not a blocker for the code): notes/20/F033.md 'What breaks if this is wrong' lists the accumulator bug only as a 'known limit'. When F033 is re-queued, the note should say that the pragma was a compile error before and is a silent miscompile for reductions without the pass fix, and name the fixing task.
